correctness.rationale: The polar is the intersection of 20 explicit halfspaces from cube vertices and four apex candidates. The supplied determinant-based algorithm identifies active quadruples, symbolic rational feasible vertices and facets on both intervals (0,2) and (2,infinity), then computes oriented 4-volume sums over full boundary simplices. We examined these finite symbolic certificate operations and independently enumerated polar vertices and primal/dual convex-hull volumes at 7 heights across the break, matching both rational formulas and polar vertex counts 20,18,24. Strictness reduces to -A(t)>0 on (0,2] and B(t)>0 on [2,infinity); independent substitution generated positive-coefficient polynomials 10432u^6+55040u^5+110656u^4+111872u³+60864u²+17024u+1920 and u^7+33u^6+418u^5+2668u^4+9216u³+16888u²+14848u+5216. Endpoint consistency t=2 and limiting 32/3 follows from formulas. Finite hull samples only cross-check; universal statement relies on the intervalwise exact symbolic inequalities and determinant checks.

originality.rationale: The original Shen–Dubovski Corollary 4 introduces this exact 4D apex pair but proves the 32/3 comparison only for 0<t<=12/7 via a sufficient estimate; the exact all-height formulas and t=2 transition are not stated in its inspected full text. Other 4D Mahler computations in Resultary concern different cube/cross-polytope/symmetric families, not a general theorem dominating this exact P_t.

value.rationale: Closes a natural all-height variation of a published sharp symmetric Mahler model, with exact primal and polar volumes and a genuine combinatorial transition at t=2. This is a motivated one-parameter extremal certificate in an open four-dimensional subject, not a claim of the universal symmetric Mahler conjecture.

limitations: No conclusion for general centrally symmetric 4-polytopes.
At t=2 combinatorics changes and both closed expressions must be checked at the common endpoint.
